source_review.notes: Checked all fifteen primary references and confirmed successful retrieval. CNCF and DORA platform guidance, NIST and CISA acquisition/supply-chain guidance, SLSA and OpenSSF provenance/project evidence, FinOps lifecycle economics, and Google SRE operational guidance support the bounded current claims.

evidence: Reviewed sourcing-option, horizon, discounted cost, mandatory-gate, scenario, consequence and exit-asset notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates monetized lifecycle estimates from qualitative consequence and treats feasibility as a constraint rather than a score.

evidence: Executed the sourcing audit and reproduced options=3, feasible=2, TCO values 1140/940/770, lowest quote buy, lowest feasible TCO adopt, exit readiness 2/3 and gate=pass.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All totals equal acquisition quote plus five declared lifecycle components; the economically cheap buy option is excluded by its failed mandatory exit gate.

evidence: Verified discounted TCO summation, mandatory-gate product, scenario-cost framing and per-asset exit predicates against their prose interpretation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formulation consistently uses a common horizon and keeps non-monetizable consequence outside false scalar precision.

evidence: Reviewed no-action, zero-price, scale shifts, tier cliffs, failed mandatory gates, vendor acquisition, maintainer loss, license change, shared dependencies, proprietary exports, permanent pilots, unsupported forks, SLA credits, data deletion and supplier failure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage includes economic, technical, operational, security, legal, community, concentration, lifecycle and exit boundaries across internal and external options.

evidence: Traced outcome, economic, assurance, accountability, reversibility and adaptation invariants through requirements, option generation, trials, contracting, operation, review and exit.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariants prevent product-led problem redefinition, asymmetric costing, compensated mandatory failures, outsourced accountability, paper portability and sunk-cost lock-in.

evidence: Verified the two-option counterexample in which a zero-license option incurs integration, operations, support and proprietary-exit cost exceeding a positive-license portable option.
proof_review.notes: The construction correctly refutes purchase price as sufficient evidence of lowest lifecycle cost.

evidence: The lowest-price counterexample is explicitly labeled as a proof sketch and states the limited sufficiency claim it refutes.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No TCO horizon, option set, assessment artifact, score or sourcing preference is represented as a universal theorem.

evidence: The sourcing audit is explicitly synthetic and disclaims universal decision use; examples are scenarios; source retrieval is dated; no real vendor, community or organizational outcome is claimed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Normative mechanisms, illustrative arithmetic, external guidance and hypothetical cases are kept distinct from empirical observations.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed outcomes and contracts, full option sets, authority, horizons/scenarios, TCO, unit economics, fit, architecture, reliability, assurance, supply-chain health, contracts, exit, customization, trials, decisions, ownership, realized outcomes and reassessment.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementability through critical-journey contracts, mandatory gates, production-shaped trials, common cost workbooks, license/provenance checks, operational escalation, contract clauses, provider adapters, export/reconstruction/deletion exercises, transition ownership and event-driven review.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified required order, one-page review, definitions and formulas, twelve-step mechanism, six invariants, bounded proof sketch, executable audit, eighteen trade-offs, thirty misconceptions, ten examples, ten connections, fifteen references, and five answered exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
